educationalGoal:
This course is separated into following two parts.
The “PC Assembly and Network” part aims to foster the knowledge and skills needed to build a personal computer from parts and construct a simple network.
In the "Physical Computing" part, students are required to create an original system consisting of I/O devices connected to a microcomputer and learn about practical interaction designing.
advice:
"PC Assembly and Network"
 In this part of the course, the following experiments and exercises will be conducted: assembly of a standard desktop PC, configuration of the BIOS, installation of an operating system, assembly of the LAN cable, building and configuring Ethernet networks, connecting to local networks using a HUB, building servers, and troubleshooting.

“Physical Computing”
 The goal of this part of the course is to realize a human-oriented interaction through experiments designed to create many kinds of interactions using I/O devices connected to a microcomputer.
 Students are required to participate actively in the class and engage in teamwork. Safety must be observed at all times. Compliance with scheduled actions and careful treatment of the equipment and tools are also required. All items must be restored to their original conditions when the class is over. Copyright infringement related to class work is strictly prohibited.
 To pass this course, students grade points must exceed 60% for each part. If any point is less than 60%, the student will fail the entire course.

              This course is separated into following two parts.
The “PC Assembly and Network” part aims to foster the knowledge and skills needed to build a personal computer from parts and construct a simple network.
In the "Physical Computing" part, students are required to create an original system consisting of I/O devices connected to a microcomputer and learn about practical interaction designing.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              "PC Assembly and Network"
 In this part of the course, the following experiments and exercises will be conducted: assembly of a standard desktop PC, configuration of the BIOS, installation of an operating system, assembly of the LAN cable, building and configuring Ethernet networks, connecting to local networks using a HUB, building servers, and troubleshooting.

“Physical Computing”
 The goal of this part of the course is to realize a human-oriented interaction through experiments designed to create many kinds of interactions using I/O devices connected to a microcomputer.
 Students are required to participate actively in the class and engage in teamwork. Safety must be observed at all times. Compliance with scheduled actions and careful treatment of the equipment and tools are also required. All items must be restored to their original conditions when the class is over. Copyright infringement related to class work is strictly prohibited.
 To pass this course, students grade points must exceed 60% for each part. If any point is less than 60%, the student will fail the entire course.
